# The Cartographer's Apprentice

## Prologue: The Map That Wasn't

The old woman had been dead for three weeks before anyone noticed the map was wrong. It hung in the back of her shop, framed in tarnished brass, and showed a coastline that did not exist. Ships that followed it never returned. Ships that ignored it arrived early, which the harbormaster found suspicious in a way he could not articulate.

Her apprentice, a boy of fourteen named Eren, had inherited the shop and the map along with it. He did not believe the stories. He believed in ink, in paper, in the steady rhythm of a compass dragging a line across parchment. He believed that maps were honest things, and that the world outside them was the one that lied.

The first time he touched the map, the room tilted. He did not tell anyone. He sat down on the shop's only chair and waited for the feeling to pass, and when it did not pass, he waited longer.

## Chapter 1: The Commission

A woman arrived on a Tuesday with a commission and a name she did not give. She wanted a map of the northern coast, she said, and she wanted it drawn by hand. She paid in silver that was older than the coins usually circulating in that part of the city. Eren noticed this and said nothing.

He began the work that evening. The coastline came easily. The rivers came easily. But when he reached the point where the old woman's map had shown its impossible harbor, his pen stopped. He had not told it to stop. It stopped anyway.

## Chapter 2: The Harbor

The harbor was real. He knew this the way one knows a face in a crowd — not by evidence, but by recognition. He drew it slowly, and the drawing took three days, and when it was finished the map on the wall had changed.
